description: Flat, hard-edged vector geometry on a near-black ground, built from a tiny primitive vocabulary — equilateral triangles, squares/rounded squares, and circles — composited with heavy transparency so overlaps read as tonal steps rather than as outlines. The palette is severely restricted: warm charcoal background, a ladder of neutral greys, and one bone/cream highlight; there is no gradient, no texture, no colour, and no line work except the edges of the shapes themselves. Almost every token is a single radial cluster around one centroid, centred in the frame with generous margin — a swarm orbiting a core — and only two or three let elements bleed past the edge. What the twelve share is that centroid-and-orbit logic, the alpha stacking, and the palette; what separates them is which primitive dominates (triangle swarms in 9011/10264/10622/10801/10980, square swarms in 9548, circular/discoid bodies in 9369/9906/10085, a hexagram core in 9190/9727), the count (three loose shards up to forty overlapping ones), the scale of the dominant form (a thumbnail-sized cluster against a full-frame disc), and the value polarity — most are light shapes on black, but 9369 inverts to a pale disc carrying a dark rosette. Across the three conditions the same object persists and its behaviour changes: neutral is the mixed state (a core plus surrounding debris), stress consolidates — debris disappears, the remaining forms grow larger, brighter and more opaque, and the silhouette becomes clean and singular — and recovery re-fragments, returning more elements than neutral, dispersed wider and at lower contrast, with 9369 additionally growing a second concentric ring.
seenAt120: The silhouette survives for the tokens with one dominant body: the cream hexagram (9190), the pale disc with dark iris (9369), the lens (9906), the teardrop/marker (10085) and the large right-pointing triangle (10801) each still read as a specific object and are instantly distinguishable from one another. The sparse and low-contrast tokens fare worse — 9011, 10443, 10622 and 10264 flatten into a generic impression of 'a few grey triangles scattered', and the two darkest (10264, 10980) sink toward the background and lose most of their internal structure. Overlap tonality survives as flat value blocks rather than as legible layering; small satellite shards below roughly four pixels drop out entirely.
